Sohlberg — alongside Shin Bet chief David Zini and Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara — said that not all details of the probe can be revealed, but that "the claim that the evidence currently before us could overturn the election results as a whole is incorrect." The CEC has repeatedly said that the scope of the investigation is limited in nature, and that the results of the vote are not in question.
Dean Livne, director general of the Central Elections Committee, told Kan that there is "no basis for the claims of election theft."
Qatar rejected the allegations, calling them "ridiculous and dangerous." "We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome," Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari said in a statement.
